*Thinking as the farmer...*

Well, I've been working this land for 45 years now, so I have a pretty good sense of what it wants. My husband and I are the only two left on the farm — the children moved to the city long ago. So labor is really my biggest worry these days, not the agronomy. I finished senior high school, which was unusual for a girl my age, and I've been to a few of those county extension training sessions over the years. I read the posted guidelines from the agriculture bureau, but honestly, after four and a half decades, I mostly know what works on my specific plots.

Of my 9 mu, I keep **6 mu in wheat-maize double cropping** — that's the backbone, it gives us food grain and reliable cash. The other **3 mu I still plant to cotton**, though I'll tell you, at my age the cotton picking is getting very hard. I've thought about switching it all to wheat-maize, but cotton still brings in more cash per mu when prices hold, and I've got regular buyers from the ginning station. So I hire two women from the village for about two weeks during picking in September-October.

**For the wheat (harvested in early June):** I apply about 18 kg N/mu total, split as base fertilizer at sowing (compound NPK 15-15-15, around 40 kg/mu) and topdress urea at jointing in March (about 15 kg/mu of urea). Soil here has decent phosphorus built up from years of compound fertilizer, so I don't add extra P beyond what's in the compound. I'll irrigate at overwintering, jointing, and booting — three times if rain cooperates, four if it's dry. Expected yield around 480 kg/mu based on last year's 500 kg/mu, slightly conservative because the fall was dry.

**For summer maize (right after wheat, mid-June):** The turnaround is always tight — we do no-till direct seeding with a hired planter, costs about 30 yuan/mu but saves days. I use Zhengdan 958 or similar hybrid, compound fertilizer at planting (about 40 kg/mu) plus one urea topdress at V8-V10 (about 12 kg/mu). That's around 16 kg N/mu total. I'll irrigate once at tasseling if July rain is short. Target 520 kg/mu.

**For cotton (planted late April):** This is where I'm most cautious with inputs because cotton prices have been unsteady. I use about 12 kg N/mu, with some base compound and a topdress at squaring. Pest pressure for bollworm and aphids means I spray 3-4 times through the season. I irrigate twice — once at squaring, once at boll-filling. Target 280 kg/mu lint.

Total I'll budget about **4,200 yuan** for inputs plus maybe **1,800 yuan** for hired cotton labor. We have some savings and the wheat subsidy, so cash flow is manageable, but I don't buy any more fertilizer than I need.
